packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-12 - unverified first reading from images only
No prior identification of the work/author was visible in my context. I did nothing beyond the brief's rules (I listed the packet directory to get image filenames/sizes only; did not open packet.json).

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001, overview, face A)
- Orientation: portrait, upright. Object is a narrow vertical strip of paper (or two strips laid side by side with a vertical gap/fold line at center; the right-hand strip is partly a separate piece, and the lower left portion is a separately mounted piece starting about a third of the way down, slightly offset leftwards). Held by clear plastic weights.
- Single block of text, cropped on BOTH left and right: lines are cut mid-word at left and right edges. So this is a slice out of a wider written page (likely a recycled document strip, e.g. binding waste).
- Language/script: German, cursive Kanzlei/Kurrent hand in brown-black ink; one top line in a larger, more formal (Fraktur/textualis-like) script: "...nbs vnd im obern ...ntal" - a heading or first line of a document.
- Punctuation: frequent virgules (/) and double-stroke hyphen/line-end marks (,, or =) at line ends.
- No rubrics, no columns, no enlarged initials visible beyond the larger script top line. A few looped strokes / flourishes in left margin area around mid-height (probably descenders or a crossed-out line). Pencil shelfmark at bottom left: "Stams, STA, Fog. 57 h(?)" (modern).
- About 40 lines of text visible on this face.
- Tiles 002-004 presumably cover this face top/middle/bottom at native resolution.

TILE image-002.jpg (native, top of face A, overview lines ~1-16)
Physical notes: left and right edges of text are cut; a vertical clear strip/fold runs down the middle (letters under it partly hidden, marked [..]). A horizontal tear line crosses l.5 left and l.9-10. Upper right corner folded. Line numbers counted from top of this image.
002.01  [tops of flourished ascenders of a cut line above; no letters legible]
002.02  ..nbs vnd Im obern? [..]nntal        (larger formal display script; "obern" partly under the strip)
002.03  ..h Vnnsers. Gotshau[s?] [V?]rbar vnd
002.04  ..ragner / vnnd Maria / [..]teiner? kalchen?
002.05  ..nigen? / [..]e? hennach? [..]tkhst? / Leiblichen? /   (tear/stroke runs through left part)
002.06  ..n / Welliches alles / bei? vnnd Amein? ,,
002.07  ..rt Wonhofers Prunnwissl? / Gegen
002.08  ..en Kirchgassens? / an d[..]ymmen? da ,,
002.09  ..lang (vormalts? Maratsch? hofs) mit ,,   (closing parenthesis visible after "hofs")
002.10  ..ch Erbrich? [..]chers / de[n]? [W?]eiggartten? ,
002.11  , vnnd auch in disen Maratschhof? ,
002.12  ..n Mittag an Mangerbau? Wein ,,
002.13  ..l hafen? [K?]anrrhörig? / vnnd des Weg ,,
002.14  ..ergenhalb / Hannß Hebst[..]chers? / an d[..]
002.15  ..gen Mitternacht / an [..]ther? genannt
002.16  [line cut at bottom edge of tile; continued in next tile]
Notes: "vnnd" written with double n throughout; ",," double hyphen at line ends = word carried over. "Mittag" / "Mitternacht" are compass directions (south/north) -> appears to be a property boundary description (observation of words, tentative).

TILE image-003.jpg (native, middle of face A)
Overlap: 003.01-003.03 = 002.13-002.15 (same lines; not new text). From 003.06 down the left side is a separately mounted lower piece, offset leftwards (its left cut edge shows more text start). A long brown pen stroke (curved line) crosses 003.07-003.08 from left margin up to the strip - possibly a cancellation stroke or a later scribble.
003.01  ..l hasen? Zuegehörig? / vnnd des Weg ,,      (= 002.13; first word could be "hafen"/"hasen")
003.02  ..ergenhalb / Hannß Hebst[..]chers / an d[..]  (= 002.14; given 003.11 "Morgenhalben", the cut word is likely [..]genhalb, tentative)
003.03  ..gen Mitternacht / an [..]ther? genannt ,     (= 002.15)
003.04  ..lben / daß hieuorbeschriben / an Man? ,,
003.05  [pen stroke from left]  Kasters? Acker / vnnd obgeschrib ,,
003.06  ..rich Hollers? / an den [..]bühel? / anstossen? .
003.07  ..n gehörig ,   [long pen stroke]   [..]ftan? / gegen
003.08  ..der Gemainweg / vnnd an Dinkhl?
003.09  ..er / der in daß [F?]ogm[..] [blot] gehörig /
003.10  ..isen vermelten? Maratscher hof / ge ,,
003.11  ..n / Daran stoßt Morgenhalben / d[..]
003.12  ..in hieuoristen? / Ivy? deß [F?]ogmer
003.13  ..[K?]ein? hingemelten? [K?]rautgartte[n]?     (last letters struck/overwritten)
003.14  ..thalb an Gemaingen? Weg / d[..] Im
003.15  ..r Stern? Cheraunzen? / [..]ebigenhait? ,
003.16  ..bs tauobrit? / den benanten hof mit
003.17  ..n vnnd Gotshaus[..] ob[..]meltten? / Ir? obenelhren?   (heavily uncertain right half)
003.18  ..erzigest? / Do ist aber [n?]achmals [..]ayh?   (bottom line, letters' lower parts cut)
Notes: "Gotshaus" reading at 003.17 is from capital G with loop like 002.03. "Maratscher hof"/"Maratschhof" recurs (002.09, 002.11, 003.10) - reading of this proper name is tentative (Mar-at-sch).

TILE image-004.jpg (native, bottom of face A)
Overlap: 004.01-004.04 = 003.15-003.18 (re-read here with full letter bottoms).
004.01  ..r Stern? Cheraunzen? / [..]ebigenhait? /     (= 003.15)
004.02  ..bs tauobrit? / den benanten hof mit       (= 003.16)
004.03  ..en vnnd Gotshaus[..] / [..] obernlehren?   (= 003.17; "obern" + word with superscript mark over -u-)
004.04  ..erzigest? / Do ist aber nachmals Zwey[ch]?   (= 003.18)
004.05  Maß / daruon gerai[..]en? / vnd dz der
004.06  ..widerumb Hube[..]? vnd? Herrnschaf[t]? .
004.07  ..dt bleiben lassen / aber darneben vns /
004.08  ..n auch auß vilgedachten hof / Järlich /
004.09  Mer zu [vor?]behalt darvon / [..]es? derselben
004.10  ..rd geraicht werden / ohn allen abgang /
004.11  ..[struck]er / drei Fasnachthenn? / Zehen Ayr /
004.12  ..rghkunnen? / ainen Todtfal geben /     (left word underlined or struck through)
004.13  ..hngenärde? /  [large looped flourish]  Vr[khun?]d deß zu Warem
004.14  ..nd Seligmachers [G]eburt? fünff[..]? ,,
[below: blank paper; looped flourish of a paraph/signature at bottom left edge; modern pencil "Stams, STA, Fag.(?) 57 m(?)"]
Notes: Ending formula visible: "Vrkhund? deß zu Warem ... Seligmachers geburt" = closing/dating clause of a charter (tentative interpretation from words); the year is cut at right. Dues listed: Fasnacht hens, ten eggs, Todtfal (heriot). Face A therefore appears to be the text end of a document.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-005, overview, face B = reverse)
- Shown landscape (rotated 90 deg relative to face A). Same two strips, now lying horizontally one above the other, with a clear tape/strip join between them.
- Two grey rectangles cover the left part of each strip (masking applied in the image, not part of the object).
- Surface largely blank: no main-text writing visible at overview scale. Faint show-through of the other face's ink at right. Modern pencil shelfmark written vertically on lower strip, left-centre: "Stams, STA, Fag.(?) 57 v(?)". Paper has vertical crease/cut lines at regular intervals (folds of a binding strip).
- Tiles 006-008 should be the native views of this face.

TILE image-006.jpg (native, left part of face B)
Blank paper; no ink text. Grey masking rectangles cover upper-left parts of both strips. Only marks: a few small stains/spots, a stray fibre/hair, vertical cut/crease lines, and modern pencil shelfmark written vertically at right: "Stams, STA, Fag. 57 v". Nothing to transcribe.

TILE image-007.jpg (native, centre of face B; overlaps 006 at left - same pencil shelfmark visible)
Blank surface. Only faint grey show-through of face A's writing (reversed) at right on both strips, not readable as text on this side. Small pinholes/knife nicks at the fold lines, stain along upper strip's horizontal fold. No writing on this face to transcribe.

TILE image-008.jpg (native, right part of face B; overlaps 007 at left)
Blank surface apart from faint reversed show-through of face A ink and a small patch of repair tissue/tape at right edge. Fold stain along upper strip, knife nicks at folds. No text to transcribe.

SUMMARY / LIMITATIONS
- Areas read: all ~40 lines of face A (tiles 002-004), every line attempted. Face B is blank (overviews/tiles 005-008).
- Text is a German-language cursive document (charter/contract-like): heading line in larger formal script "..nbs vnd Im obern [..]nntal"; then a boundary description using compass terms (Mittag, Mitternacht, Morgenhalben), neighbours' names (Hannß Hebst[..]chers, [..]rich Hollers, Wonhofers), places (Maratsch(er) hof, Gemainweg, [K]rautgarten?), then obligations ("Järlich ... ohn allen abgang ... drei Fasnachthenn / Zehen Ayr ... ainen Todtfal geben") and a closing clause "Vr[khund?] deß zu Warem ... Seligmachers [G]eburt fünff[..]" with the date cut away. These are observations of words; no work/author identification attempted.
- Every line is truncated at both left and right edges (strip cut from a wider sheet), so no sentence is complete; a vertical clear repair strip in the middle obscures 1-3 letters per line. Personal and place names are the least secure readings.
- Lower left piece (from 003.06 down) is a separately mounted fragment; its alignment with the upper lines appears continuous but should be checked.
- A wider image of the sheet (if the rest of the document survives elsewhere) would be needed to complete lines.
